logline: A superhuman young woman raised in Mongolia returns to Seoul's Gangnam to find her mother and ends up dismantling a billion-dollar drug empire.

seasons.review_body: Strong Girl Nam-soon aired October through November 2023 on JTBC, also streaming on Netflix internationally. A spin-off of the 2017 hit Strong Girl Bong-soon, the series introduces a new superhuman protagonist raised in Mongolia who returns to Gangnam in search of her parents and gets drawn into a drug investigation. The finale peaked at 10.42% nationwide, reinforcing the franchise's commercial pull. Tonally, the series strains between its action-comedy premise and its darker drug storyline, and the mismatch drew notice from the Korean entertainment press. Lee Yoo-mi’s physical commitment in the action sequences stands out, while the three-generation super-strength family dynamic delivers moments of genuine warmth. Byeon Woo-seok’s stylish villainy also helped drive a social media surge, even as some plot mechanics felt less satisfying.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Strong Girl Nam-soon Season 1 Episode 1 aired October 7, 2023 on JTBC and Netflix as the premiere of the 16-episode series. The finale recorded 10.42% nationwide on Nielsen Korea. The series is a spin-off of the 2017 Strong Girl Bong-soon, written by the same writer Baek Mi-kyung. The premiere efficiently establishes the franchise mythology across three generations of superhuman women and installs Nam-soon's specific origin: raised in Mongolia after being separated from her Gangnam family, she returns to Seoul with no blueprint for the city and considerable ability to reshape its infrastructure. Lee Yoo-mi's physical commitment in the action sequences reads immediately, and the first demonstration of Nam-soon's strength in Seoul traffic is staged for deadpan comedy in the manner the original series established. The premiere sets up the drug cartel investigation thread that will occupy the season, alongside the family reunion arc, combining genre registers with the same tonal ambition and tonal inconsistency that defined the 2017 original.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere efficiently establishes the superhuman family mythology across three generations and sets Nam-soon's origin - abandoned in Mongolia, impossibly strong, searching for identity. The Gangnam setting is deployed with comedic self-awareness. Lee Yoo-mi makes an immediate impression as a physically committed, warmly played lead.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Nam-soon's first casual display of superhuman strength in the middle of Seoul traffic - played for deadpan comedy in a way the original series earned.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.review_body: Strong Girl Nam-soon Season 1 Episode 16 aired November 26, 2023 on JTBC and Netflix as the series finale. The finale recorded 10.42% nationwide on Nielsen Korea - strong cable numbers for the franchise. The finale delivers the action-heavy setpiece confrontation the drug cartel arc has been building toward, with the production's physical stunt work deployed at full scale. Lee Yoo-mi's superhuman action sequences land as the episode's primary technical achievement. The family reunion resolution provides the emotional counterweight the season has been promising, and it delivers with more warmth than the crime procedural thread achieves in its resolution. The domestic cable performance confirmed strong audience attachment to the franchise even when critical reception was mixed on the gap between premise and execution. The 10.42% figure makes the finale the season's peak, suggesting audience investment that outlasted structural reservations.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves the drug cartel arc with action-heavy setpieces that showcase the series' visual ambitions. The family reunion elements land emotionally, though the crime procedural threads resolve more mechanically. The 10.42% finale rating confirmed strong domestic audience attachment.
